newsitem.title: USA: G&K to buy some National Linen assets.
newsitem.headline: G&K to buy some National Linen assets.

text.p: G&K Services Inc said Monday it had signed an agreement to purchase the uniform rental assets, plus selected linen rental assets, of National Linen Service, a division of National Service Industries Inc.
The purchase price will be about $287 million cash, subject to adjustment after a post-closing audit.
G&K said the acquisition will strengthen its position in the southeastern U.S. and make it the third largest supplier in the uniform leasing industry.
It said it expects revenues for fiscal 1998, beginning July 1, will be in excess of $500 million from continuing operations after the acquisition.

G&K said it will acquire 29 National Linen processing facilities, including 20 uniform rental plants, five linen rental plants and four mixed uniform and linen rental plants. All but five of the plants are located in the Southeast.
The 20 uniform rental facilities have annual revenues of about $125 million. The nine other plants have annual revenues of about $80 million.
G&K already operates 32 plants in the U.S. and Canada, with reported revenues of $341 million during the most recent four quarters.
The transaction has been approved by the boards of directors of both companies and is subject to closing conditions including approval under U.S. antitrust law.
G&K said the closing is expected within six weeks.
It has obtained bank commitments to facilitate the financing of the acquisition and the refinancing of its existing bank and other debt.

"This acquisition presents a tremendous opportunity for G&K," Richard Fink, chairman, said in a statement. "Added to our existing business in the Southeast, it will give us a leading market presence in this rapidly growing region."
He said G&K will evaluate the strategic potential of each acquired facility to determine whether it should be retained as a G&K operation.

G&K, which historically has focused on uniform leasing, said the acquisition will enable it to leverage corporate programs over a broader revenue base and compete more effectively for large regional and national uniform accounts.
"In addition, the increased revenues will allow us to scale back our planned investments in start-up ventures over the next several years," Fink said.
G&K sees "great potential" to improve the performance of the acquired uniform plants over the next few years, he said.
